title: Launch risk coordination — blockers, rollback plan, and incident comms package
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Coordinate cross-functional launch risk activities for runtime-1.28. This ticket centralizes release blockers, the rollback plan, and all incident communications artifacts to ensure we can launch with clear gating, recover quickly if something goes wrong, and communicate transparently with customers and internal stakeholders.

Scope:
- Track and drive closure of critical release blockers across Eng, Design, SRE, and Legal.
- Produce a verified rollback playbook with step-by-step procedures and ownership for each rollback path (service-level, region-level, model-variant fallback).
- Finalize incident communication templates (customer-facing status, internal incident channel, exec summary) and pre-approve legal/PR language.
- Ensure monitoring and alerting dashboards are configured and tested, and that oncall handoffs are scheduled.

Current blockers (action owners inline):
1) KV cache cold-start flakiness causing TLS timeouts on some regions — blocker owner: ENG-2719 (SRE); mitigation: temporary prefix-priming script; gating: run 72h soak in staging.
2) Rollout routing policy lacks region fallback for EU customers — owner: ENG-2801 (routing); mitigation: add explicit region fallback rule; gating: routing e2e test green.
3) Release notes embargo and legal sign-off not confirmed — owner: Legal review (Design provides copy); gating: Legal approval required 48h before launch.

Rollback plan (overview):
- Level A (fast automated): automatic model-variant fallback to lower-capacity quantized model if token error rate >0.8% for 15m or lat95 increases >250ms. Owner: Serving Runtime oncall.
- Level B (manual, service): full service traffic reweight to dedicated pool in another region (30% -> 0% over 10m), performed by SRE lead with PM approval. Owner: SRE.
- Level C (full rollback): rollback release artifacts and model pin to prior runtime-1.27 image. Requires runbook execution and a post-rollback assessment. Owner: Release Engineering + PM.
- Verification steps after rollback: synthetic canary tests, top-customer smoke checks, and notify customers within the hour.

Gating criteria for advancing each rollout stage:
- Pre-launch: all P0 blockers closed or documented mitigations + legal approval + oncall dry-run completed.
- Canary -> Ramp: no new P0 incidents for 30m at 10% traffic and error/latency thresholds within SLOs.
- Full: 24h stable canary + release notes published and comms scheduled.

Incident communications package:
- Internal channel template (Slack #incidents): short summary, immediate impact, current mitigation steps, owner, ETA for next update.
- Customer status template (status.redwood.ai): succinct impact, affected customers, what we are doing, next update ETA, and workaround if available.
- Executive one-pager: short impact summary, customer lists (top 10), and recommended next steps for GTM.
- Post-incident public postmortem checklist with timelines and who drafts follow-ups.
(Links to drafts below, legal/PR already flagged for review.)

Tasks and owners:
- PM (assignee): finalize comms templates, coordinate legal/PR sign-off, own go/no-go decision timeline.
- ENG: close ENG-2719 and ENG-2801; produce rollback scripts and automated rollback tests.
- SRE: run oncall dry-run of rollback runbook and validate alerts/dashboards.
- Design: finalize release notes visuals and customer-facing language (DES-512).

Decision log / trade-offs:
- We decided to keep an automated model-variant fallback rather than full traffic rollback as first line because it reduces blast radius and is faster to execute; trade-off is potential temporary quality degradation which we will mitigate by preferring higher-quality quantized variants.
- Chosen canary size: 10% initial to surface infra issues while minimizing customer impact; larger canaries would surface issues faster but increase customer risk.

Acceptance & verification:
- Confirm that synthetic canary tests exercise KV cache warm paths.
- Verify alert thresholds and run a simulated incident to test comms templates.
